requirements.title: Cognitive (IQ) testing — comprehensive, with all scores
requirements.parentLabel: A full test of how your child thinks and learns

attributes.failReason: Kit couldn't find a comprehensive intelligence test OPWDD accepts (for example a WISC or Stanford-Binet). Brief or screening measures like the WASI or KBIT won't substitute.
OPWDD wants the report to include all summary scores — full scale, index, and subtest — not just an overall number.

recency.note: OPWDD's guidelines require 'current' evaluations without publishing a hard age limit. 36 months is Kit's working interpretation; reviewers often request newer testing, as they did in real cases.

citations.where: Section II.C.2 (Required Documentation); Section III.E (Appropriate Standardized Assessment Measures); Appendix A p.25-26
Documentation required: psychological report with assessment of intellectual functioning

explanations.partially_supported: {docTitle} looks like the right kind of document, but {reason}
explanations.not_found_in_current_corpus: Kit didn't find comprehensive IQ testing in the documents it has. It may exist somewhere Kit hasn't seen.
explanations.stale_or_wrong_stage: {docTitle} exists, but {reason} OPWDD reviewers often ask for more recent testing.
explanations.suggestedAsk: Ask the evaluating psychologist for the final, signed report of a comprehensive intelligence test (e.g., WISC-V) including full-scale, index, and subtest scores. OPWDD asks for ALL available cognitive testing, not just the newest.

requirements.title: Adaptive behavior assessment — standardized, with interpretive report
requirements.parentLabel: A standardized look at everyday skills (like the Vineland)

attributes.failReason: Kit couldn't find a standardized adaptive measure OPWDD accepts (Vineland or ABAS).
OPWDD wants composite, domain, and subdomain scores reported, plus a narrative written by the clinician — a computer-generated score sheet alone is not accepted.

recency.note: OPWDD requires 'current' adaptive evaluation without a published hard limit; 36 months is Kit's working interpretation.

citations.where: Section II.C.2; Section III.C (2.0 SD criteria); Section III.E; p.12 (interpretive report required, computer-generated reports not accepted); Appendix A p.26

explanations.partially_supported: {docTitle} looks like the right kind of document, but {reason}
explanations.not_found_in_current_corpus: Kit didn't find a standardized adaptive assessment (like Vineland or ABAS) in the documents it has.
explanations.stale_or_wrong_stage: {docTitle} exists, but {reason} OPWDD reviewers often ask for more recent testing.
explanations.suggestedAsk: Ask the evaluator for a Vineland-3 or ABAS-3 with composite, domain, and subdomain scores AND an interpretive report written by the clinician. OPWDD asks for ALL available adaptive assessments.

requirements.title: Comprehensive autism evaluation (when eligibility is based on ASD)
requirements.parentLabel: A complete autism evaluation — not just a diagnosis letter

attributes.failReason: OPWDD requires structured, ASD-specific measures based on licensed-clinician observation (for example ADOS-2 or CARS-2).
the report must include a comprehensive developmental history — milestones, repetitive behaviors, preoccupations, social interactions, and friendships.
the report must include an observations section describing the person's behavior during the evaluation in detail, plus which specific autism symptoms are present and how they show up.

recency.note: No hard published limit; reviewers requested a current comprehensive autism evaluation in real cases.

citations.where: Section II.C.5; Section II.E (ASD requires comprehensive evaluation, not a single screening); Appendix A p.26 (Autism paragraph)

explanations.not_found_in_current_corpus: Kit didn't find a comprehensive autism evaluation in the documents it has. A diagnosis letter alone does not satisfy this — OPWDD wants the full differential diagnostic assessment.
explanations.suggestedAsk: Ask for a comprehensive autism diagnostic report that includes ADOS-2/CARS-2 (or similar structured measures), a full developmental history, an in-evaluation observations section, and the specific symptoms with behavioral descriptions.

requirements.title: Medical / specialty documentation supporting the qualifying diagnosis
requirements.parentLabel: Medical records that back up the diagnosis

attributes.failReason: the report must state the qualifying diagnosis, how it was arrived at, and how it impacts functioning.

citations.where: Section II.C.1; Appendix A p.25 (Medical Documentation) and p.26 (Medical Reports and Specialty Assessments)

explanations.not_found_in_current_corpus: Kit didn't find medical or specialty reports supporting the qualifying diagnosis (required when the diagnosis is something other than intellectual disability).
explanations.suggestedAsk: Ask the diagnosing provider for the report that states the qualifying diagnosis, how it was reached, and how it affects your child's functioning — signed by the clinician.

requirements.title: Evidence for the LCED decision criteria
requirements.parentLabel: The three things the waiver form actually checks
requirements.decisionLogic: Eligible for ICF/IID Level of Care if: (1) documented qualifying diagnosis made or approved by a physician — AND — (2) disability manifested prior to age 22 — AND — at least one of: (3) severe behavior problems endangering self or others; (4) health care need (daily individualized medical attention, self-injurious behavior, or self-care skill deficits); (5) adaptive behavior deficit in any of: Communication, Learning, Mobility, Capacity for Independent Living, Self-Direction.

attributes.failReason: Kit hasn't seen evidence speaking to the LCED criteria yet.

citations.where: p.4-5 (Determination of Eligibility: Q1 AND Q2 AND (Q3 OR Q4 OR Q5)); p.8-12 (definitions of each question, including the five adaptive deficit areas A-E)

explanations.needs_qualified_review: Your documents contain evidence that speaks to these criteria — {evidenceSummary}. Whether it satisfies the form is a judgment for the QIDP and reviewing physician or nurse practitioner, not for Kit. Kit's job is making sure they have everything in front of them.
explanations.not_found_in_current_corpus: Kit hasn't seen documents that speak to the LCED criteria yet — the cognitive, adaptive, and behavioral evidence above usually carries this.
explanations.suggestedAsk: Ask the care manager to confirm the QIDP has the full record — the LCED is completed by a qualified professional and reviewed and signed by a physician or nurse practitioner. OPWDD's own staff complete this form; your job is supplying the evidence.
